paragraphs.heading: A day in a blindfold
paragraphs.edited: In college, I had a chance to be a resident assistant, a rep in charge of fun activities and events on a floor. To help us have some compassion and understanding for students on our floor who might have handicaps, the leadership decided that we would go around for a day with a handicap of sorts. My handicap was to wear a blindfold.

Well, to help us have some compassion and understanding for students on our floor who might have handicaps, the leadership decided that we would go around for a day with a handicap of sorts. paragraphs.edited: It really dawned on me for the first time, since I had to go to the cafeteria and I had to go to class with this blindfold on, how tough it is to navigate life without sight. How did I cope? How did I make it through the day? I had to ask somebody to help me. Who did I ask? I didn't ask a stranger. I didn't ask somebody I just met. I asked somebody I trusted, one of my basketball teammates, to help me out through the day.

paragraphs.heading: Faith is not blind
paragraphs.edited: People often have the idea that faith is blind, and that when it comes to issues of religion, it's like we're frolicking around in the dark and basing our beliefs on sheer ignorance. This might be true for some religions, but it is not true for Christianity. You see, biblically, faith is trusting what we have reason to believe is true. Just as I followed the guidance of my friend whom I had good reason to trust when I was blindfolded, God asks us to follow him, and he's given us good reasons to trust him. We are not called to blind faith.

paragraphs.heading: Why did they come to Jesus?
paragraphs.edited: You might be thinking, wait a minute, didn't Jesus do the miracle because of the man's faith? After all, it says in Mark chapter 2 that Jesus, seeing their faith, pronounced to the man, son, your sins are forgiven. Now, it is true that God often does reward our faith by performing miracles. But let's ask a more basic question. Why did these four men and the paralytic come to Jesus in the first place? The answer is because, as Mark 1 tells us, Jesus had already been performing miracles. Jesus had already been casting out demons. He had given them evidence and signs that he's the Son of God, so they came to him with confidence and put a faith in him that was well placed.

paragraphs.heading: Come, let us reason together
paragraphs.edited: Jesus calls people to love God with their heart, with their soul, with their strength, and with their minds. In the Old Testament and in the New Testament, God calls people to an intelligent faith, and he still does the same today.

paragraphs.heading: Why John recorded the signs
paragraphs.edited: This is why in the Gospel of John, a gospel which is written recording the miracles of Jesus and inviting people to a confident faith, at the very end of the gospel John writes, in chapter 20 verses 30 through 31, that Jesus performed many other miracles not even recorded in this book. But they've been recorded so we might have confidence that Jesus is the Son of God, he's the Christ, and that by believing in him we may experience eternal life. The Gospel of John is written so we understand who Jesus is based on the miracles, so we can have a confident faith, and by having that faith experience eternal life.

paragraphs.heading: Investigate the evidence
paragraphs.edited: Biblical faith is not blind. The Bible invites non-believers to investigate the evidence, to consider the claims of Christ, and then to consider believing in him. And as Christians, we're also not called to a blind faith. We are called to think deeply about our faith, to know why we believe what we believe. We are called to have an answer when people ask us the reason for the hope we have within.
